tier_reason: First-party hyperfine output in the README Performance section (regorus eval 4.6 ms +/- 0.2 ms vs opa eval 45.2 ms +/- 0.6 ms on tests/aci); commands and policy files are public and the README gives the cargo release build command, but hardware, OPA version and rustc version are not stated, so not A, and no independent measurement was found.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Cargo release profile via 'cargo install --example regorus --path .' (README); rustc version and OPA version/build unstated
corrections.workload: README Performance section: hyperfine on 'regorus eval -b tests/aci -d tests/aci/data.json -i tests/aci/input.json data.framework.mount_overlay=x' vs the same 'opa eval' command line, whole-process timing of both CLIs (regorus 422 runs, OPA 62 runs).
corrections.caveats: Whole-process timings of two CLIs: Go runtime startup and per-invocation policy compilation probably account for much of OPA's 45 ms (OPA user time 68.8 ms exceeds its 45.2 ms wall time, so it ran multi-threaded), so the evaluation-only ratio is unknown; the README's in-process ACI test times (cargo test -r --test aci, about 3.6-5.0 ms per test) have no OPA counterpart such as opa bench. No hardware, OPA version or rustc version stated; benches/aci_benchmark.rs is a Criterion benchmark of regorus only, with no OPA comparison. Single policy (Azure Container Instances) and single query. Regorus does not yet support all OPA builtins (README: mostly compliant with OPA v1.2.0). Rego is a policy language, not one of the category's general-purpose interpreter baselines.

notes: README numbers match the record exactly (about 10x, derived from page data). Shortcomings: CLI whole-process timing that includes Go startup, one policy and one query, no hardware or versions, in-repo Criterion bench measures regorus alone. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 350 stars, 542 commits, last commit 2026-10-01, not archived.

tier_reason: Upgraded from D: the README chart is unreadable here (user-images.githubusercontent.com EGRESS_BLOCKED), but issue #140 (third-party user esrrhs, 2021-06-25) posts per-benchmark seconds from the repo's own benchmark set for pocketlang, Python and Lua 5.3.4; no hardware, Python version or pocketlang build mode, so numbers without methodology, tier C. Benchmark code is public (tests/benchmarks/*, scripts/run_benchmarks.py).

corrections.baseline: CPython (version unstated in issue #140) and Lua 5.3.4; the README chart (image only) compares against CPython 3.7.4, Ruby MRI 2.7.2 and Wren 0.3.0
corrections.claimed_speedup: Issue #140 (third-party run, 2021-06-25), pocketlang vs Python seconds: factors 4.00 vs 5.27 (1.32x faster), fib 3.04 vs 3.03 (parity), list 2.88 vs 2.59 (0.90x, slower), loop 1.23 vs 2.20 (1.79x faster), primes 3.74 vs 2.91 (0.78x, slower) (ratios derived from page data). Lua 5.3.4 was 3.2x to 6.8x faster than pocketlang on every benchmark. The README's own bar chart (pocketlang pre-alpha vs Wren 0.3.0, Python 3.7.4, Ruby 2.7.2) could not be read here.
corrections.hardware: Unstated for the issue #140 numbers; the README chart was run on Windows 10 64-bit, ASUS N552VX, Intel Core i7-6700HQ 2.6GHz, 12GB RAM
corrections.workload: Five benchmark programs in tests/benchmarks/ (factors, fib, list, loop, primes; a tco directory exists but is not in the runner list) run by scripts/run_benchmarks.py, which times each interpreter via the 'elapsed: <time>s' line each script prints; Node.js is deliberately excluded from the runner.
corrections.caveats: Only readable numbers are a 2021 third-party GitHub issue with no hardware, Python version or pocketlang build mode: pocketlang beat CPython on 2 of 5 benchmarks (loop, factors), tied on fib and was slower on list and primes, and Lua 5.3.4 was 3-7x faster than pocketlang on all five. The README chart (pre-alpha pocketlang vs Wren 0.3.0, Python 3.7.4, Ruby 2.7.2, i7-6700HQ) is an image that could not be read here; compiler and flags not stated. Timing comes from each script's self-reported elapsed time, not an external harness. Development effectively stopped in June 2022; the only later commit (2026-01-03) adds native API documentation and build-system changes.

notes: Shortcomings: not faster than CPython on 3 of 5 benchmarks in the only readable run (issue #140), Lua 3-7x faster, README chart unreadable and on old versions, no compiler flags. Tier raised D to C on the issue #140 numbers; if the orchestrator prefers the README as the anchor, keep D and carry the issue numbers as a caveat.
